name: Port Neill
reason: Seaside village with the Eyre Peninsula's largest jetty, 1 km main beach and the 4.5 km Lady Kinnaird walking trail (searched; Wikivoyage Eyre page only mentions it as a bus stop, so the guide source is the web-found weekendnotes/tourism listings). Second-tier harbour town stop.

name: Venus Bay
reason: Town wrapper: the draw is Venus Bay Conservation Park, listed separately; no counted source names the village itself as a stop.

name: Baird Bay
reason: Wikivoyage Eyre Peninsula names swimming with sea lions at Baird Bay as a highlight; the bay is the place, the operator's boat (Jones Island) is how you reach the experience, to be said in the bio.

name: Cummins
reason: Tourism board lists the free, always-open Cummins Mosaic Trail through town (self-guided public art walk), a half-hour-plus walk; one counted source, a minor stop. Consider naming the spot Cummins Mosaic Trail.

name: Nullarbor Roadhouse
reason: A roadhouse is a business; searched southaustralia.com and Wikivoyage Nullarbor, which treat it only as a fuel stop and no counted source names a sight (the plain sign is a photo stop).

name: Border Village
reason: For: roadside icon (Big Kangaroo) at the WA border, a classic photo stop. Against: Wikivoyage Nullarbor says Border Village is a roadhouse with little to offer, and I found no counted source naming the Big Kangaroo; it is a business and a short stop.

name: Koppio
reason: Town wrapper: the draw is Koppio Smithy Museum (National Trust, 2.5 acre site), which should be judged under its own name; the locality alone has no counted source.

name: Spalding Cove
reason: A campground cove inside Lincoln National Park; the parks page names no walk or lookout there, no distinct draw beyond the park.

name: Surfleet Cove
reason: A campground cove inside Lincoln National Park; the parks page names no walk or lookout there, no distinct draw beyond the park.

name: Sleaford Bay
reason: SA Parks insider tips name Sleaford Bay Road lookouts and Lincoln NP viewpoints for southern right whale watching; surf beach in Thorny Passage Marine Park.

name: Sleaford Mere
reason: Searched parks.sa.gov.au and Wikivoyage: no counted source names the saline lake as a place to visit.

name: Cape Wiles
reason: Headland on the Whalers Way coast with no counted source naming it; covered by Whalers Way.

name: Mikkira Station
reason: Wild koala sanctuary on a farm west of Port Lincoln listed as an attraction by southaustralia.com; access by permit/gate key from the Port Lincoln visitor centre (cooler months self-drive, tours year-round).

name: Axel Stenross Maritime Museum
reason: Tourism board lists the boatbuilding museum with original workshops and working slipway, open Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun, $8 entry; a real hour-long visit.

name: Port Lincoln Railway Museum
reason: Small volunteer museum open Wednesday 1-4pm only, one counted source; no real chance of a visitor arriving to find it open (rule 4 in spirit) and a short visit.

name: Port Lincoln Old Mill
reason: Tourism board: 1846 Old Mill, the oldest structure in Port Lincoln, free lookout tower over Boston Bay with a rose garden; second-tier town sight.

name: Winter Hill Lookout
reason: Tourism board describes it as a popular panoramic lookout over Boston Bay, Lincoln NP and Spencer Gulf; free and open.

name: Flinders and Freycinet Lookout
reason: Short interpretive pull-out above Port Lincoln with one source; a minor roadside lookout (rule 3), given Winter Hill and the Old Mill cover the views.

name: Mighty Mulloway Sculpture
reason: Tourism board lists the bronze mulloway sculpture by Ken Martin at the Y-Stop Yalata Roadhouse on the Eyre Highway (not Port Lincoln, correct the placement): a quirky roadside icon. Short stop.

name: Port Lincoln Street Art Trail
reason: Tourism board lists a free, self-guided, walkable mural trail through Port Lincoln, always available.

name: Parnkalla Trail
reason: Tourism board and the Lincoln NP parks page describe the coastal walk and cycle trail along Boston Bay to Lincoln National Park with lookouts and headlands.

name: Westall Way Loop
reason: The page now loads and names the stops on the 32 km unsealed scenic loop: Smooth Pool, High Cliffs, Granites and Cape Bauer Lookout; free coastal drive near Streaky Bay.

name: Neptune Islands
reason: Wikivoyage Eyre Peninsula and NPWS name the islands as the great white shark cage-diving destination off Port Lincoln. No landing, seen from operator boats; per 'a spot is a place' the island is the spot and the operators are mentioned in the bio. Close call.

name: Golden Island Lookout
reason: Searched the Coffin Bay NP parks page: it mentions only Golden Island Beach in a shark alert and does not name a lookout as a sight; part of Coffin Bay National Park.

name: Almonta Beach
reason: Wikivoyage Coffin Bay lists Almonta Beach among the park's places to go; surf beach in Coffin Bay NP (part 4WD access).

name: Mount Dutton Bay Woolshed Museum
reason: For: State Heritage-listed 1875 woolshed with restored stone buildings and museum, listed by the tourism board, $10. Against: private property, tours by phone booking only and vary seasonally, one counted source.

name: Anxious Bay
reason: A bay label: searched Wikivoyage, tourism board and parks pages; no counted source names it as somewhere to go.

name: Venus Bay Conservation Park
reason: Parks SA and the tourism board both list it: Weyland Peninsula beaches, tombolo, bird life and fishing; free conservation park open to visitors.

name: Sceale Bay
reason: southaustralia.com lists Surfers Beach at Sceale Bay, with lookouts, swimming and surf lessons, 28 km south of Streaky Bay; small coastal village stop.

name: Laura Bay Conservation Park
reason: Tourism board and parks page describe the sheltered bay with mangroves and samphire flats, bird feeding grounds, lookout and 1911 landing site; free, half-hour visit.

name: Streaky Bay Museum
reason: Wikivoyage Streaky Bay See lists the National Trust museum with historic vehicles and local history.

name: Streaky Bay Powerhouse Museum
reason: Tourism board calls it a must-visit: 400+ restored working engines; open Tue and Fri 2-5pm only, so note hours in the bio. Close call on opening days.
